newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Farmer sales behind last year.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Farmer sales behind last year.

text.p: Hot, dry weather across southwest and south-central Kansas was seen ensuring harvest progress remained rapid on Tuesday but recent price weakness kept farmer sales slow, dealers said.
They noted farmers were just selling enough wheat to look after their short-term cash flow needs.

"We're below $3.00 at a lot of places in the country and that is such an important psychological level they (farmers) are going to sit on it (their wheat) for a while," one Kansas dealer said, noting sales were much slower than last year.
Isolated two cents cash protection was reported.

Most grain dealers were however looking for a modest bounce after the recent decline in values. KCBT July wheat futures on Monday fell to the lowest level for the nearby contract in almost three years.
July closed at $3.30-3/4 a bushel, which equated to less than $3.00 a bushel at Kansas locations such as Colby and Dodge City.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
